title.narrative: REACH: Evidence-gathering on community perceptions, priority needs and preferences in Sri Lanka

participating-org.ref: UK - Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office

recipient-country.narrative: As of July 2022, Sri Lanka is facing an economic crisis rooted in high inflation, fuel shortages and low foreign exchange reserves. The UN Humanitarian Needs and Priorities (HNP) Plan (launched 09 June) estimated 5.7 people in need. While many, including WFP and FAO , expect a deterioration of the situation, there is still an absence of critical sources of information on community priorities in terms of humanitarian assistance as well as perceptions of ongoing programming among affected people. Moreover, humanitarian decision makers are faced with a critical gap of information on the differential impact of the crisis on various groups of people, especially in terms of how the compounding multi-dimensional crisis is exacerbating pre-existing vulnerabilities through a loss of access to resources and reduction in access to essential services among persons with disabilities, older people, female-headed households, persons with critical illnesses and others. To support response actors to prioritize and plan with enhanced awareness of community preferences in terms of humanitarian assistance and modalities of assistance, REACH proposes to launch a participatory assessment focused on Accountability to Affected People. The assessment will seek community triangulation of the assumptions that underly the current humanitarian response in terms of what the drivers of the crisis are, how the crisis is impacting the lives of people in crisis-affected areas, and what solutions should be pursued and supported by humanitarian actors from the point of view of local actors and affected people. The assessment would also aim to identify geographical areas and population groups that are particularly impacted by the crisis and whose needs and priorities should be monitored more closely by the response. REACH also proposes to collaborate with OCHA / the ISCG in country to facilitate a joint analysis session once preliminary findings are available, involving both the conventional coordination and response actors, such as ISCG members and key operational agency representatives, and local civil society organizations, including women-led groups, organizations of persons with disabilities (OPD), older people’s associations (OPA), and others. The proposed activities are based on discussions with key actors operating in the country (OCHA, WFP, NGO consortia). Activities are also based on REACH’s previous experience responding to over 30 humanitarian crises and addressing critical information gaps in similar crises to Sri Lanka, including a growing portfolio of activities focusing on amplifying community voices through community engagement, as well as accountability to affected people.
